messages.subject: Unable to process large MSI object
messages.subject_clean: Unable to process large MSI object
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a v. large MSI object (from 36 combined experiments resulting in  255,342 pixels and 38,683 features) so I am running into problems when trying to apply processes to it - specifically;
combinedDataMinFreq <- combinedData %>%
  peakFilter(freq.min=0.05) %>%
  process()

To mitigate this I was thinking to subset features (ca. 1000  features per object) from my main MSI object and run the peakFilter process on these objects separately and then combine the result.
In essence I suppose this is what should be happening if I register as a multicore but that doesn't appear to work either unfortunately.
Is there a function similar to cbind() which would allow me to combine MSI objects with same pixel space but different features?

Of course a more simple solution would likely be to apply a more strict minimum frequency on the images before combining - but ideally I would like to apply it this way too.

Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: Unable to process large MSI object
messages.subject_clean: Unable to process large MSI object
messages.body_plain:
Hi Matt,

is your problem that you don't have enough RAM for the calculation or do you get a specific error message. If so please post it here.

Unfortunately currently there is no other combine option than cbind(), which requires the mz axis to be the same. If you only filter but not centroid your data you could bring them back to the same axis with the mzBin function.

HTH,
Melanie

messages.body_plain:
Yes it is - I get  “Memory cgroup out of memory” as readout from the fail from the slurm cluster.

I did manage to find a way to manually parallelize the job as several separate jobs and return a vector of m/zs to keep then subset the MSI object using the vector.

When using the inbuilt  parallelization I get the following error:
in result[[njob]] <- value : attempt to select less than one element in OneIndex In addition: Warning message: In parallel::mccollect(wait = FALSE, timeout = 1) : 1 parallel job did not deliver a result

Could this be an out of memory error too? As it runs correctly in serial and parallel if the MSI object is split into smaller chunks...

Best wishes,
Matt

messages.subject: Extract intensity of mass ranges
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I've recently started working on MSI data and my project requires the extraction of the intensity of several ions to compare their abundances in different samples.
Although I have learned with the help of this group how to extract the intensity of one ion, I still haven't figured out how to extract a range of ions.

Example: I have a tissue section and I want to extract the intensity of m/z 1523.758+- 0.003, so I would need to have the intensity values of this m/z range: 1523.755 - 1523.761, and not only the one from the main ion 1523.758.

Is there a way to do it?

Here is the line of code I'm stuck with:
###
intensity <- spectra(file)[features(file, mz=1523.758),]
###

Then I can go ahead and convert this into a data frame, but I would only get the intensity values of the selected m/z and not of the 'surrounding' ions.

Thanks in advance for the help!

Giulia

messages.subject: Error in valid object
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kylie,

Am getting an error like shown below, what does it mean and how to resolve it?

Error in validObject(x):
   invalid class "atoms" object: 'offset' contains negative indices

Best,
Nivedita
messages.body_snippet:

Best,
Nivedita

messages.subject: Re: Error in valid object
messages.body_plain:
This is either an error from an older version of 'matter' (that should be fixed on all recent versions) when reading larger imzML/ibd files, or it indicates that the imzML file may have been improperly written. First, check that you are on a current version of Cardinal/matter; if you are, then try running the imzML file through imzMLValidator (https://gitlab.com/imzML/imzMLValidator) to see if the issues are in the file itself.

-Kylie
